newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit retreats on technical, fund sales.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit retreats on technical, fund sales.

text.p: The ringgit retreated in post-lunch Asian session as funds covered short dollar positions, triggering stop losses around 2.4870 a dollar, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Once beyond 2.49, there was a technical rebound, which pulled down dollar/ringgit again," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
She said a few interbank players, who had been bidding up dollar against the ringgit for the last few days, managed to push beyond 2.49 in thin midday trading.
At 0800 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4887/97 a dollar.

The dealers said the ringgit retreat to below 2.49 was expected after the over two percent gain since the start of the year. However, sentiment remains in the Malaysian unit's favour in the medium-term, they added.

The ringgit was also ailing from rumours of a trade deficit for November, 1996. In a poll by Reuters on Tuesday, economists from 10 research houses forecast an average deficit of 148 million ringgit for November.
"Once the correction is over, funds will come back to the Malay because they want to establish positive yield positions," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
